lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: needs, wants, and priorities

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 4
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G4 Unit 1 — choices, scarcity, and tradeoffs
objective: Learners sort an invented month of spending into needs and wants, total each group, and test the combined plan against a fixed pretend amount to see what priority order protects.
scenario: Ayana is a made-up fourth grader planning a pretend month with $60.00 of simulated money. Her invented list holds two needs, a $24.00 bus pass and $18.00 of lunch supplies, and two wants, a $9.50 game and a $6.25 poster.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Total the two invented needs on Ayana's list: the $24.00 bus pass and the $18.00 of lunch supplies.

prompts.text: What do Ayana's needs cost together?

tasks.directions: Now total the wants separately, then bring both groups together against the $60.00 Ayana has for the pretend month.

prompts.text: What do Ayana's wants cost together?
What does Ayana's whole plan cost?

tasks.directions: Ayana checks the finished plan against her $60.00, then finds out the bus pass has gone up to $27.00 while everything else stays the same.

prompts.text: How much of the $60.00 is left under the original plan?
With the $27.00 bus pass, how does the plan compare with Ayana's $60.00?

tasks.directions: The price rise fell on a need, not a want.

prompts.text: Ayana has to cut something. Which item would you cut first and why does priority order matter more than which item she likes least?

remediation: If a learner cuts by preference, cover the price column and have the learner write, for each item, what would go wrong for Ayana without it, then restore prices and cut only from the items with no consequence attached.
extension: Ask the learner to rebuild Ayana's plan under the $27.00 bus pass so it fits $60.00 exactly, showing the totals for both groups.
